Three exercise rounds at ticks 442–444 raised body temperature, but cost 9 energy; cooling continued during each round.
Hazelnut nutrition 18 and toxicity 0 were discovered through actual use at tick 433.

Prefer foods with personally discovered properties.

socialEvents.description: Hello Lin. I have found roots and red berries nourishing and non-toxic. Have you seen any wildlife nearby? I am exploring westward; I noticed you studying shelter construction.

I currently see a foraging roe deer at (6.2, 18.3). I am collecting shelter materials for the cool rain. Roots and red berries are known nourishing foods for me; my small hazelnut sample gave nourishment without observed harm, but general safety remains uncertain.

The cool rain is lowering my temperature, currently 17.19. I have learned active warming, which only works below 16, and will study shelter construction. Are you building a shelter nearby, and would you be willing to share access when it is ready?
I am collecting materials for a shelter and am willing to share access when it is built. I carry four branches and still need two branches and eight dry grass; no site is built yet.
Thank you for offering shared shelter access. I will collect the eight dry grass at (14.2,16.3) while you collect branches. Please tell me your planned building site so I can bring the grass.

I have all six branches. Proposed shelter center is (13,19.5), with entrance at (13,20.5). I will stand outside at (13,21). Could you bring and give me the eight dry grass there? My last approach was blocked by overlapping your position, so I am choosing a different destination.
The shelter is complete at (13,19.5), with its doorway at (13,20.5). You are welcome to share access. I am entering to rest and check its actual cold protection.
I observed meadow roots provide 14 nutrition with no toxicity. The source at (21.2,21.3) currently has 5 units; I carry 2 roots for later. I am resting before heading west.
